title: Cataract Surgery in the Post-Radial Keratotomy (RK) Eye
summary: Managing cataract surgery in post-RK eyes requires navigating profound corneal instability, irregular astigmatism, and high risk for IOL power calculation errors. This guide outlines the evidence-based strategies for achieving successful refractive outcomes and maintaining structural integrity.

data.title: Cataract Surgery in the Post-Radial Keratotomy (RK) Eye
data.summary: Managing cataract surgery in post-RK eyes requires navigating profound corneal instability, irregular astigmatism, and high risk for IOL power calculation errors. This guide outlines the evidence-based strategies for achieving successful refractive outcomes and maintaining structural integrity.

sections.title: Clinical Overview & Challenges
sections.content: Radial Keratotomy (RK), popular in the 1980s and 90s, utilized radial incisions to flatten the central cornea. As these patients age, they present for cataract surgery with unique anatomical issues: extreme corneal flattening, diurnal refractive fluctuations (corneal instability), and a high likelihood of refractive 'surprises' post-operatively due to inaccurate biometry.

sections.title: The Pathophysiology of Post-RK Optics
content: Peripheral incisions weaken the corneal biomechanics, leading to progressive hyperopic shifts over decades.
Non-physiologic 'oblate' corneal shape (flatter in center, steeper in periphery).
Significant increase in Higher-Order Aberrations (HOAs), especially spherical aberration.
Diurnal Fluctuation: Incision edema causes corneal steepening (myopic shift) in the morning and flattening (hyperopic shift) in the evening.

sections.title: IOL Calculation: Why Standard Formulas Fail

rows: Standard K-readings assume a fixed ratio between front and back corneal surfaces (37.5/337.5). RK alters this ratio.
Underestimation of corneal power → Hyperopic Surprise
Keratometers measure at 3.2mm, often missing the flatter central optical zone (flat-top profile).
Underestimation of corneal power → Hyperopic Surprise
Formulas (like SRK/T) use K-readings to predict the Effective Lens Position. Flat K leads the formula to expect a shallow AC.
IOL placed too posterior relative to calculation → Hyperopic Surprise

sections.title: Recommended IOL Power Formulas
content: Barrett True-K (No History or History): Currently the gold standard; utilizes the Barrett Universal II and a modification for the oblate cornea.
Haigis-L: Uses 3 constants (a0, a1, a2) and doesn't rely on K to predict ELP, making it more accurate in post-refractive eyes.
Shammas-PL: No-history formula that adjusts the measured K to account for the post-RK geometry.
Potvin-Hill: Utilizes Pentacam (Scheimpflug imaging) measurements of the central 4mm zone.
ASCRS Post-Refractive Calculator: Essential tool for averaging multiple advanced formulas.

sections.title: Pre-operative Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Perform serial topography/tomography to ensure refractive stability (difference <0.5D over 3-6 months).
Step 2: Measure at the same time of day (preferably late afternoon when cornea is flattest).
Step 3: Obtain axial length using optical biometry (IOLMaster 700 / Lenstar).
Step 4: Use Pentacam/OCT to find the 'True' central corneal power.
Step 5: Counsel patient extensively on 'Refractive Neutrality' vs 'Refractive Precision'.

branches: Scleral Tunnel: Preferred for 8+ incisions or peripheral RK to avoid intersecting scars
Clear Cornea: Only if 'safety zone' between RK incisions is >2.5mm
Avoid Incision Intersections: Prevents 'fish-mouthing' and dehiscence
Side-port Meticulousness: Use a sharp knife; avoid tearing existing RK scars

sections.title: Intraoperative Considerations
content: Low Flow / Low Bottle Height: Prevents excessive stress on weakened cornea.
Liberal Use of OVD: Disperse-and-Cohesive (Soft-Shell) to protect the endothelium.
Gentle Hydrodissection: Avoid high-pressure fluid waves that might stress incisions.
Capsulorhexis: Standard size (5.0-5.5mm) to ensure IOL stability.
Wound Closure: Check for RK incision leaks (Seidel test) even if they weren't directly touched.

rows: Best Choice (e.g., SofPort AO, enVista). Doesn't add to corneal HOAs.
Caution. May worsen vision if centration is poor or HOAs are high.
Generally Contraindicated due to loss of contrast sensitivity.
Use only if astigmatism is regular and central (rare in post-RK).
Excellent for irregular astigmatism / high HOAs.

sections.title: RED FLAGS: The Hyperopic Surprise
content: Most post-RK refractive errors result in unwanted hyperopia.
Targeting -0.75D to -1.25D (Myopic target) is MANDATORY to compensate for late hyperopic shift.
Intraoperative floppy iris or poor visualization due to RK scar light scattering.
Rupture of RK incisions ('Fish-mouthing') during phacoemulsification.
Small Optical Zones (<3mm) signify high risk for severe irregular astigmatism.

sections.title: Management of Incision Dehiscence
content: Step 1: Immediate reduction of IOP/Infusion pressure.
Step 2: Close the dehiscence with 10-0 Nylon sutures (X-pattern or interrupted).
Step 3: Ensure the suture is buried and not inducing excessive astigmatism.
Step 4: Use a bandage contact lens (BCL) post-operatively.

content.explanation: F: Formulas (Barrett True-K, Haigis-L). L: Late-day measurement. A: Aim for Myopia (-1.0D). T: Tunnel Incision (Scleral).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Under-promise and over-deliver: Patients must expect a 'two-step' process (Phaco then Enhancement).
Double-K Method: Use the pre-RK 'K' to calculate ELP, but the post-RK 'K' for lens power calculation.
Wait at least 8 weeks post-op before finalizing refractive measurements or performing enhancements.
Always look for 'macro-gaps' in RK incisions under the slit-lamp pre-op; these are high risk for dehiscence.

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Evidence
sections.content: The ASCRS Post-Refractive IOL Calculator study (Wang et al.) demonstrated that the Barrett True-K and Haigis-L formulas significantly outperform traditional third-generation formulas (Hoffer Q, SRK/T). The PERK Study (Prospective Evaluation of Radial Keratotomy) provided the long-term data showing the 10-year progressive hyperopic shift (mean +0.89D) that clinicians must account for when choosing a myopic target in cataract surgery today.
